In perhaps his most famous appearance, this character is in front of a television labeled "television" that shows a building labeled "U.S. munitions works" and is (*) falling onto a booklet marked "sabotage plans for U.S.A." For 10 points, name this character who is being punched in the face on the cover of Captain America Comics #1, the boss of the Red Skull who appears in Fantastic Four as the Hatemonger.

An author with this surname, who frequently used the phrase "The Power of One," wrote a profile of an aerospace engineer who was the target of a smear campaign after co-founding Caltech's Jet Propulsion Laboratory. A park in San Jose honors an author with this surname who is the dedicatee of R. F. Kuang's grimdark fantasy The Poppy War and a time-travel story by Ken (*) Liu. Hate mail and death threats resulted in the 2004 suicide at age 36 of that author with this surname, who used her own grandparents and the diaries of Minnie Vautrin and John Rabe ("RAH-buh") as sources for a 1997 bestseller that alleges thousands of mass murders were covered up by Japan's government. For 10 points, give this surname of the historian who wrote The Rape of Nanking, Iris.

3.q: This man served as a consultant on the Strategic Visions strategy game, BARIS. Navy Admiral Bud Scoles was once his AA sponsor, a detail related in his addiction memoir, Magnificent Desolation . With John Barnes, he co-wrote a sci-fi novel that imagined using solar winds to achieve near-light speeds titled Encounter with Tiber. In 2002, he punched (*) conspiracy theorist Bart Sibrel in the jaw. His television appearances include playing the true love of Liz Lemon's mother on an episode of 30 Rock and accompanying Race Banyon on a mission saved by an inanimate carbon rod. This man served as the Lunar Module Pilot on a mission with Michael Collins. For 10 points, name this second man to walk on the Moon.

For ten points, name this novel about the bounty hunter Rick Deckard written by Philip K. Dick.

3.q: A Broadway musical based on this comic strip by Gene De Paul and Johnny Mercer originated the song "If I Had My Druthers." In this comic strip, which originated the terms double whammy and Lower Slobbovia, Kickapoo Joy Juice was produced by Hairless Joe and Lonesome Polecat. This comic strip parodied Dick Tracy with a strip-within-a-strip called Fearless Fosdick. An animal shaped like a (*) bowling pin who would gladly produce almost any food was called a shmoo in this comic strip, which also inspired the name of Lockheed Martin's "skunkworks". This comic strip invented an occasion where women would ask men out to a dance in November, Sadie Hawkins Day. For 10 points, name this comic strip created by Al Capp, in which Daisy Mae marries into the Yokum clan of Dogpatch.

The Ultimate version of this character was originally meant to be a cure for cancer, while further experimentation with its cells in that universe produced a creature that killed and resurrected a person living with this creature's greatest enemy. For reasons of insanity, this character was exiled to battleworld by its own kind where it was (*) picked up by its greatest enemy during the Secret Wars storyline and briefly worn before its sentient nature was discovered by Reed Richards, leading this villain to be forced off through the resonance of church bells. Although Mac Gargan, the Scorpion, has been one of its hosts, its best-known host is a disgraced journalist who failed to find the identity of the Sin-Eater, Eddie Brock. For 10 points, name this black and white symbiotic enemy of Spiderman.

3.q: One of this man's articles was expanded by computer scientist Charles H. Bennett in 1982, and this man published the short story collection The Voice of the Dolphins. This man first observed that cobalt could be used to create a salted (*) nuclear weapon with especially deadly fallout, a version of which was adopted as the "Doomsday Device" in Dr. Strangelove. In a 1929 paper, this man argued that the need to acquire information would result in a violation of the Second Law of Thermodynamics if Maxwell's Demon were to exist. Along with Fermi, this man patented the neutronic reactor, but he is most associated with an idea that came to him while he was walking to work in London waiting for traffic lights to change. For 10 points, name this Hungarian physicist who first described a nuclear chain reaction.
